question.text: A sponsor debates between PARALLEL and MASTER-FEEDER structures. Parallel is GENERALLY MORE EXPENSIVE than master-feeder because:

answer.text: Parallel requires SEBI pre-approval for every trade

In parallel, each fund (onshore AIF + offshore fund) has its own separate investment manager and charges a full management/performance fee, duplicating cost layers; in master-feeder, fees are largely centralised at the master level with only a nominal fee at the feeder
Parallel funds must pay higher SEBI registration fees
Parallel structures are not allowed to use custodians

explanation.text: The Logic: In parallel structure, each vehicle has its own investment manager and full fee layer — two managers, two fee stacks. In master-feeder, fees are largely centralised at the master level with only a nominal fee at the feeder. Investors in parallel end up paying two layers of fees indirectly, making it generally more expensive than master-feeder. The Trap: Options A, C, D are fabricated. The cost differential comes from the duplicate fee layers when offshore managers in a parallel structure provide investment management services to each vehicle. Note: Per the workbook (pages 129-131), master-feeder centralises fee charges at the master, while parallel structures duplicate manager-level costs across the onshore AIF and the offshore fund.
